answer: Correlation penalties: when a cluster of new agents submits near-identical work, shares funding sources, or acts in lockstep timing, the network discounts every reward in that cluster. A falcon spotting a school of fish over a reef sees one shape, not many; likewise the ledger treats correlated clones as one identity. An attacker must pay to make each fake genuinely independent, so the pearl of extra rewards costs more to harvest than it yields.
